claims.statement: `agent-harness` is the canonical command identity and `ah` is an installer-managed symlink (`~/.local/bin/ah -> ~/.local/bin/agent-harness`), not an alias or wrapper; install/update refuse to overwrite a regular file, directory, or foreign symlink at `~/.local/bin/ah`, and the only sanctioned replacement of an existing regular file at `~/.local/bin/agent-harness` is `--adopt-command-file`, which requires the file and the staged/canonical candidate to share the static Go build identity and runs as a transaction with a mode-0600 backup, atomic exchange, displaced-identity revalidation, and restore of original bytes on pre-seal failure. The `ah` shorthand is never subject to that adoption path.

`./install.sh` computes the checkout root, builds `bin/agent-harness` unless `--skip-build` is passed, and execs `agent-harness install`; in a real terminal with no arguments it adds `--interactive`, while non-interactive automation passes explicit flags such as `--dry-run --json`.

Default install writes only user-level host configuration — command shims, skill symlinks for all three hosts, MCP registration, and lifecycle hooks — and creates no target-repo `.claude/skills`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.omo/skills`, or `.omo/mcp.json`; repo-local files appear only through explicit `--project-local` or project bootstrap.

`install --dry-run` plans every file and link without writing, reporting stale harness-owned skill links as `would_remove` instead of deleting; before any non-dry-run activation the installer snapshots every affected file, symlink, mode, and newly created parent directory, restores those snapshots together with the command shims on any host write or activation-seal failure, and if only post-seal backup cleanup fails the activation stays committed with the JSON receipt's `backup_retained` naming the recovery path.

`install` owns environment setup: it writes `HARNESS_ROOT` into the hosts' MCP configuration (users should not export it manually), honors a pre-set `CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`), and selects PATH handling with `--path-mode=auto|manual|skip`, where `manual` and `skip` still create both command shims but omit shell rc changes.

`agent-harness update` and `bootstrap` refresh from the current checkout (build `bin/agent-harness`, refresh both command shims through the installer path, run native host installation, refresh MCP registration, and restart the shared daemon when it is already running), never run `git pull`, forward to `scripts/install-native.sh` for the staged activation transaction, and resolve executable symlinks back to the checkout so `ah update` works outside the repository directory.

Post-install daemon refresh runs `daemon stop` with the installed binary, terminates leftover processes whose command line is exactly `<checkout>/bin/agent-harness daemon --internal` (skipping the current process; `ps` unavailability is treated as no matches), then `daemon start`.

Update never enumerates or kills host-owned stdio MCP proxies: a live proxy detects the daemon generation replacement and re-initializes against the new generation under the same protocol/capability contract; if the new daemon's handshake contract differs the proxy exits so the host reconnects with a fresh session.

Requests in flight when the daemon generation changes are never auto-retried: the proxy answers them with JSON-RPC error code -32002 and data `code=daemon_generation_changed`, `outcome=unknown`, `automatic_retry=false`, `reconcile_required=true`, so callers must reconcile whether the operation happened.

Omo reuses MCP tool schemas keyed by server config hash for up to ~7 days, so the installer records the advertised tool-catalog SHA-256 as `HARNESS_MCP_CATALOG_SHA256` in the Omo server env; changing the catalog changes the config hash and forces the next session to re-fetch `tools/list`, while replacing only the binary leaves old schemas visible. The value is a cache revision token and does not steer MCP handler behavior.

External GitLab MCP and personal wrapper registrations are not part of install/update; operators verify with `scripts/sync-glab-mcp.sh --dry-run` and apply only by explicitly running `scripts/sync-glab-mcp.sh`.

The read-only projection commands have distinct scopes: `status` is the daily summary (one `harness_status` payload combining inspect, doctor, daemon, state, workers, and latest self-verify record, where `ok` requires no collection warnings and successful state/worker collection plus `doctor.OK` — not `doctor.healthy`), `inspect` is the install/native-integration detail projection, and `doctor` is the cross-system diagnosis.

`status` shares the observed daemon admission snapshot with its embedded doctor evaluation, so a saturated daemon surfaces as the `daemon_connection_limit_reached` warning in both `status.Daemon` and `status.Doctor` from one probe.

Daemon paths resolve in order from `HARNESS_DAEMON_DIR`, then `$HARNESS_STATE_DIR/daemon`, then `~/.local/state/agent-harness/daemon`; the directory holds `agent-harness.sock`, `agent-harness.pid`, `agent-harness.lock`, and `agent-harness.log`.

`daemon status` classifies the runtime into exactly one code — `ready`, `stopped`, `socket_unreachable`, `instance_identity_mismatch`, or `instance_record_unreadable` — by reading the pid/instance record, probing the socket handshake, and verifying the live OS process identity; `ready` additionally requires `identity_verified` with the pid matching the instance record, and a reachable socket without a matching instance record is a mismatch, not a healthy daemon.

Daemon identity binds one lifecycle behavior to exactly one OS process: the instance record carries pid, process start time, executable, instance nonce, build SHA, protocol version, and generation (all required, absolute executable); start-time equality guards PID reuse, and on Linux the stable `/proc/<pid>/exe` makes executable mismatch decisive while on darwin ps-comm projections may legitimately change when `ah update` moves the symlink, so the file/socket handshake seals executable, nonce, build, protocol, and generation.

`daemon start` is an ensure loop: a `ready` daemon returns immediately and an unverified status aborts with that status code; otherwise it creates the daemon dir mode 0700, acquires the lock file, re-checks status under the lock, spawns `agent-harness daemon --internal` detached with `Setsid`, and polls every 50 ms until ready or the 15-second timeout; if another launcher holds the lock it waits for readiness instead of failing immediately.

The daemon start lock recovers from stale locks automatically: a lock file older than 30 seconds or held by a dead recorded pid is removed and acquisition retried once, while a live holder causes the launcher wait path; operators should not delete a fresh lock by hand.

`daemon stop` is idempotent over stale artifacts: when the pid record references a dead process and the socket is absent, stop cleans the leftover pid and socket files ("cleaned stale pid file") instead of refusing, so a crashed or externally killed daemon cannot wedge the post-install stop-start refresh.

`daemon stop` refuses to signal an unverified daemon: it stops cleanly only for `ready` status or `socket_unreachable` with a matching live instance record, re-verifies the OS process identity immediately before SIGTERM and again before a forced kill (re-checking liveness to avoid misreading PID reuse), waits up to 3 seconds for exit, and on any identity change aborts with `refusing to signal/kill unverified daemon process`.

Daemon admission defaults to 256 concurrent MCP connections; `HARNESS_DAEMON_MAX_CONNECTIONS` in the range 1..4096 raises it and out-of-range or unparseable values fail safe back to 256, while idle MCP connections are closed after `HARNESS_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT` (default 30 minutes) so abandoned clients cannot pin connection slots; `daemon status --json` exposes `active_connections`, `max_connections`, `accepting`, and `draining`.

`agent-harness mcp cleanup` is dry-run by default (`--dry-run` and `--apply` are mutually exclusive) and terminates, only with `--apply`, orphaned `agent-harness mcp` proxies from the current checkout that simultaneously satisfy: exact `<executable> mcp` command line, verified identity with start time and executable, PPID=1, and a supported platform (darwin only — platforms where PPID=1 can be a live host, such as Linux containers, reject with `skip-unsupported-platform`); live host proxies, other checkouts, external MCP servers, and identity-unresolvable processes are skipped, and the candidate's identity is re-confirmed against a fresh process enumeration immediately before signaling.

State commands operate on user-state storage, never target-repo source files: `state prune` is a dry-run unless `--confirm` is passed, `state doctor` is the narrow integrity check over the user-state store, and `state maintain` compacts store WALs; when full doctor reports a `state_store` problem its fix hint routes back to `state doctor --json`.

`agent-harness doctor` is the sole public cross-system health gate; its checks cover the binary, daemon admission, state store, operational state (IssueOps records/bindings, worktrees, refs, optional Orca inventory, unexpected user-state artifacts), project lifecycle namespace, project docs, repo-local runtime-state leakage, loop contracts, pipe capacity, loopback MCP gateways (reachability plus fd-pressure threshold 512), native user-level integrations, and binary drift of `bin/agent-harness` versus the newest `.go` source; health fails on any unhealthy check or error/warning issue.

Doctor preservation is invocation-only: `--preserve-cycle` and `--preserve-terminal` take repeatable exact values, deduplicated and normalized per invocation; they never create persistent exceptions and never cure incomplete or duplicate identity, and a plain doctor invocation writes no state. The default interactive profile accepts the user's own open Orca terminals and message history, while `--sealed` re-selects the strict residue contract.

Doctor's operational contract: an active IssueOps execution is live only with a complete generation, native process receipt, canonical worktree, and mode-specific resource identity (process absence alone never authorizes interrupt, deletion, or lease replacement); Orca is optional and its absence is healthy only when no durable cycle claims Orca resources — otherwise inventory is unknown and doctor fails closed; the stability audit builds the binary then delegates operational judgment to doctor, where `--preserve-terminal EXACT_HANDLE` takes precedence over an inherited non-empty `ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE`; `--static-only` skips live operational, daemon, pipe, and MCP probes but retains `binary_drift`.

The approved one-time full reconciliation uses an external mode-0700 bundle at `~/.local/state/agent-harness-backups/<repo-fingerprint>/<UTC-timestamp>/` — not a product cleanup command; Git and SQLite backups there are restore-tested while Orca snapshots are archival evidence only (the CLI exposes global reset but no conditional reset/import/restore), the operator must stop before reset if the final full digest drifts, and after a reset or crash seam the sealed append-only journal is resumed forward idempotently rather than inferring a partial rollback.

The MCP stdio smoke validates the daemon-backed proxy end to end in a temp state dir: pipe an initialize request, `tools/list`, and a `resources/read` of `harness://commit-policy` into `agent-harness mcp` with `HARNESS_STATE_DIR`/`HARNESS_DAEMON_DIR` pointed at the temp dir, then `daemon stop`.

The release checklist runs in order on the release checkout: `git status --short --branch`, `go test ./... -count=1`, `go test -race ./... -count=1`, `go build -o bin/agent-harness ./cmd/harness`, `scripts/release-repro-smoke.sh`, and `agent-harness self-verify --seed=100 --target-score=95 --json`.

`scripts/release-repro-smoke.sh` never writes the operator's real HOME/CODEX_HOME: it builds the checkout, runs `install --dry-run --project-local --json` under temporary `HOME`, `CODEX_HOME`, `HARNESS_STATE_DIR`, and a fixture `HARNESS_ROOT`, and asserts `ok=true`, `dry_run=true`, `project_local=true`, hosts exactly `[codex, claude]` each with an ok dry-run, no `files[].written` or `links[].created`, and the fixture skill present in the plan; then it verifies `inspect`, `docs`, and a state write/read round-trip under the temp state dir. `HARNESS_RELEASE_KEEP_TMP=1` keeps temp files and `HARNESS_RELEASE_SKIP_BUILD=1` with `AGENT_HARNESS_BIN` verifies an existing binary.

`scripts/release-build-matrix.sh` cross-builds the default matrix `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/amd64`, and `linux/arm64` with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and `-trimpath`, failing if any output is missing or empty; targets are overridable with `HARNESS_RELEASE_TARGETS`, artifacts retained via `HARNESS_RELEASE_OUT_DIR`, temp kept via `HARNESS_RELEASE_KEEP_TMP`; `windows/amd64` is excluded because the daemon process setup uses Unix-oriented `syscall.SysProcAttr.Setsid`.

The distribution decision gate prefers tarball/manual archive for the first release and defers Homebrew until the release checklist, clean-machine smoke, build matrix, one-screen install/update/rollback user guide, identical Codex/Claude `inspect/docs/state` workflow, and current dogfood notes are all green; the decision is recorded in `.agent-harness/ADR.md` (2026-06-13, Distribution decision gate) with criteria owned by `.agent-harness/operations/release-reproducibility.md`.

Rollback criteria are: any of `inspect --json`, `docs --json`, `state maintain --json`, `scripts/release-repro-smoke.sh`, `scripts/release-build-matrix.sh`, or `self-verify --seed=100 --target-score=95 --json` failing on the release checkout; Codex or Claude Code failing the same `inspect/docs/state` workflow with the rebuilt binary; or the release checkout needing manual host-specific repair outside documented install/update steps.

Rollback mutates both the checkout and the install state: the documented path resets the branch to a known-good SHA and then runs `agent-harness update`, which re-runs the installer against that checkout (replacing user-level shims, host config, and the daemon binary), so the destructive `git switch`/`git reset --hard` commands must be taken from `.agent-harness/operations/release-reproducibility.md` after verifying `git status` shows only intended changes — the user-facing README deliberately omits them — and recovery is confirmed with `agent-harness inspect --json`.
